WEB SECURITY & RELEASE ENGINEERING
Prepared by: Dhruba Poudel
Case: Purano Maidan — sports booking and community platform
Publication summary prepared: 24 November 2026
Release verification record: 21 November 2026

I developed the platform's role-aware booking and community workflows and followed the implementation into a controlled dependency-update release. The release process connected repeatable builds, regression checks, hosting verification and a retained rollback option.

CHECKPOINT                         RECORDED EVIDENCE
Dependency install                 Locked/frozen installation completed.
Application build                  Clean hosting build completed.
Regression checks                  Recorded application/build test checks passed.
Hosting adaptation                 Hosting-adapter smoke checks passed.
Public route verification          Homepage, help centre and direct venue route/refresh exercised.
Public service check               Health response and public directory API exercised.
Identity boundary                  Sign-in/reset screens exercised; unauthenticated administrator requests rejected.
Rollback preparation               Previous successful deployment retained.

DELIVERY STAGE AND ACCEPTANCE
The public platform remains a preview/controlled beta. The 21 November record verifies a maintenance release within the scope above. It does not replace full end-to-end acceptance of real customer transactions.

The release record leaves these checks for separate acceptance:
• Real email delivery.
• Authenticated transactions.
• Backup restoration.

Earlier product verification is a separate dated record: 97 application checks and a separate 33-check core API suite on 28 August 2026. These totals are kept distinct and are not presented as newly executed tests.

The case demonstrates controlled maintenance and release engineering: make the change, repeat the checks, verify the hosted surface and keep a recovery option available.
